Diagnosis.Molecular Markers: ER positive, PR positive, HER-2/neu negative

Additional Comments: The patient is a 59-year-old woman with a newly diagnosed clinical stage III invasive lobular carcinoma of the left breast. Her cancer is ER positive with 96% of cells staining, PR positive with 35% of cells staining, and HER-2/neu negative with 0 cells staining. Imaging studies, including an MRI and PET/CT scan, revealed a large mass in the left breast with associated left axillary and subpectoral lymph node involvement, but no evidence of distant metastatic disease. A fine needle aspiration of a thyroid nodule found during the PET/CT scan revealed a benign colloid type nodule. The patient has a history of hypertension, which has been well controlled with medication for 30 years, and she has undergone a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for fibroids with bleeding at age 35. She has also experienced a herniated disk at L3-4, which was treated with physical therapy and ice, resulting in no residual pain. The patient has decided to pursue a mastectomy rather than neoadjuvant hormone therapy and has been referred for surgical evaluation.
